transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Evan Carter (Head of Security, Lucent), Priya Nair (Platform Lead), Marcus Holt (VP Engineering)

Summary: security posture discovery for Lucent Financial evaluating Redwood's hosted, dedicated, and private deployment options. Focus on compliance artifacts, SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, retention policies, and network requirements.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood — Jordan from our SE team is here too. Evan, Priya, Marcus, thanks for joining. Just to set context this is a security posture discovery so we can understand your constraints for hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:15] Evan (Lucent): Yep, thanks Maya. We're evaluating multiple vendors, want to validate security controls before we move forward. High level we need SOC 2 Type II, ideally ISO 27001 as well, plus SSO and SCIM for provisioning.
[00:30] Jordan (Redwood): Totally understood. Quick intro on our side — Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and we have customers with ISO attestation; we can share certs under NDA. For SSO we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC can be scoped per-team.
[00:45] Priya (Lucent): A couple specifics: Can you support customer-managed KMS? We need to ensure keys are under our control for some regulated workloads.
[01:02] Jordan (Redwood): Yes, we support customer-managed keys in our Dedicated and Private deployments. For Hosted we offer provider-managed KMS by default and a bring-your-own-key option for enterprise plans — the technical integration varies. There's also an HSM-backed option for Private installs.
[01:20] Evan: When you say bring-your-own-key for hosted, is that KMIP/HSM or do we upload keys to your KMS? We prefer not to upload raw keys.
[01:35] Maya: Good question. For hosted BYOK we integrate via cloud KMS APIs — you keep the key in your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and we use grants/roles to encrypt data. We don't persist unencrypted key material. For fully air-gapped on-prem/private we can integrate with an HSM.
[01:50] Marcus (Lucent): On audit logs: we have strict retention requirements, also need to push logs into Splunk. How granular are the audit logs? Can we get per-request metadata and token-level usage?
[02:08] Jordan: We emit detailed audit logs — authentication events, request/response meta (we redact actual PII/payloads by default unless you opt-in), model and route used, latency, and token counts. Logs can be streamed to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3-forwarding, and retention policies are configurable.
[02:30] Priya: Retention policy — Lucent mandates 7 years for certain audit trails, is that feasible?
[02:45] Maya: Seven years is longer than our default but for Dedicated and Private deployments retention is configurable and we can arrange long-term archival to your storage bucket. For Hosted we have tiered retention; long-term archives may be via customer-managed storage. We'll follow up with specifics.
[03:05] Evan: What about encryption in transit and at rest? TLS is baseline but we need to confirm cipher suites and FIPS requirements for certain PII workloads.
[03:20] Jordan: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; for FIPS/HSM we can support FIPS-compliant stacks in private deployments. For hosted, we support TLS with recommended ciphers — we can provide cipher list and cert rotation cadence.
[03:36] Speaker 2 (Lucent): and SSO flow, do you support in-band provisioning?
[03:43] Maya: We do SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle. SCIM supports groups and attribute mapping so you can map roles to RBAC. We also support role sync and automated deprovisioning.
[04:00] Marcus: RBAC — we need fine-grained roles: admin, approver, reader, developer. Can we map those to our AD groups?
[04:15] Jordan: Yes, you can map SAML or SCIM groups to Redwood roles. In Dedicated/Private you can also configure stricter tenant isolation and network controls.
[04:30] Evan: From a network perspective: we prefer VPC peering and private control plane. Does Redwood offer a private control plane that doesn't traverse the public internet?
[04:45] Maya: For Private deployments yes, we offer a private control plane and the option to host the control plane inside your VPC/on-prem. Dedicated offers isolated compute with a customer-dedicated GPU pool, but control plane is still hosted unless you opt for our Private offering. We'll document the data flows.
[05:05] Priya: Can you describe data residency and data retention for hosted? We have EU residency needs for some customers.
[05:20] Jordan: Hosted supports region-pin for data residency (EU, US). For strict residency and air-gapped requirements we'd recommend Private; Dedicated gives you compute isolation but control plane artifacts may still be in region you select.
[05:35] Evan: Audit reports: will Redwood provide SOC 2 Type II report and ISO attestation? What's the cadence and gating?
[05:50] Maya: We can provide SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestation under NDA. The SOC 2 is annual; ISO is on the attestation cadence. We'll attach the certificates and a SOC 2 bridge letter if needed.
[06:05] Marcus: Legal also asked about contractual SLAs for uptime and incident response. For Dedicated we expect an SLA.
[06:18] Maya: Dedicated has SLA options; Private can be part of an enterprise contract. We'll include the SLA language in the follow-up.
[06:30] Evan: Integration with our SIEM — you mentioned Splunk. We want raw audit events into our Splunk. Are events encrypted and delivered with guaranteed ordering?
[06:50] Jordan: Events are delivered over TLS to your ingestion endpoint or to an S3 bucket we can push to. Ordering is best-effort; if ordering is required we can discuss sequence numbers. We do sign events and can include integrity checks.
[07:10] Priya: For on-prem deployment, what's the operational model? Who manages upgrades and security patches?
[07:25] Jordan: For Private on-prem we offer an operator model: Redwood provides the control plane package and we can coordinate upgrades, or you can manage the on-prem package with our runbooks. Patches can be automated through our orchestration or manual per your change window.
[07:45] Evan: Backups and disaster recovery — do you encrypt backups and how are they stored?
[07:55] Maya: Backups are encrypted at rest using KMS. For Private deployments backups can be stored in your object store. For Hosted we use our managed storage but can integrate customer-managed storage for long-term retention.
[08:10] Speaker 3 (Lucent): Any third-party pen-test results or vuln scanning reports you can share?
[08:20] Jordan: We run regular pentests and automated scanning; summary results can be shared under NDA. We also provide a vulnerability disclosure program and a SOC escalation path.
[08:33] Marcus: For dedicated performance: if we need low-latency inference in EU, what are our options?
[08:45] Jordan: Dedicated pools in region with pinned capacity are best; Private on-prem gives the lowest network latency. We also have edge options in partner regions for certain models.
[09:00] Evan: Are model logs retained? We want to avoid storing customer request payloads unless necessary.
[09:12] Jordan: By default we store metadata and token-level counts; payloads are not retained unless you enable retention for fine-grained auditing. You can opt into full payload retention for a subset of routes, always encrypted.
[09:30] Priya: Regarding access controls, how does Redwood handle internal RBAC? Do your employees ever access customer data?
[09:45] Maya: Access is role-based, with Just-In-Time and least-privilege. Redwood engineers require approvals and work through an audited jump host or a ticketing workflow. We provide audit trails for any support access and can do time-limited session recordings if needed.
[10:05] Evan: Legal asks about subprocessor lists and data processing addendums.
[10:15] Jordan: We'll share an up-to-date subprocessor list and standard DPA; enterprise DPAs and bespoke clauses can be negotiated.
[10:30] Marcus: On encryption algorithms, do you support AES-GCM and KMS signed keys?
[10:40] Jordan: Yes AES-GCM and envelope encryption with KMS are supported. For HSM we can use PKCS11/KMIP integrations.
[10:55] Priya: Any concerns about model drift or leakage? From a security perspective we want assurances around training data usage.
[11:05] Maya: Redwood's hosted models do not use customer prompts for training by default; we have explicit controls and opt-ins. For Dedicated/Private, you control the model lifecycle and nothing is used for cross-customer training. We can provide language for the contract.
[11:25] Evan: For compliance audits, will Redwood provide evidence like config snapshots, logs, and change history?
[11:40] Jordan: Yes, we can provide configuration snapshots, change logs, and hardened images. For Private you can host the control plane so evidence is direct from your environment.
[12:00] Marcus: Can we do a POC with dedicated pool for a month and run load + security tests?
[12:10] Maya: Absolutely — typical POCs include a dedicated pilot with restricted access and benchmark runs. We'll include assistance from SEs for the test harness.
[12:25] Priya: One last thing, how do you handle incident notifications and post-incident reports?
[12:35] Jordan: We have a SOC process, incident templates, and can provide SLA-based incident response times. We share root cause analysis and mitigation steps.
[12:50] Evan: Great. Next steps?
[13:00] Maya: Recap — we'll send SOC 2 and ISO artifacts under NDA, Jordan will follow up to schedule a technical deep dive and request sample logs, and we'll draft Dedicated/Private pricing and the proposed SLA. Priya will send network diagram. Marcus will confirm expected QPS and retention.
[13:20] Marcus: Sounds good.
[13:25] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email and put the technical deep dive on calendar.
[13:30] Call ends.

Notes on transcription: minor mis-hearings present, some speaker labels generic. Repeated phrases and filler words preserved.
